title: MMMU-medical Lingshu-7B vs 32B anomaly: investigation + faithful re-eval + method impact

root_cause.verdict: NOT a harness/parse/position artifact. Under IDENTICAL faithful MedEvalKit conditions (same 150 idx, same gold, same prompt, same parser, no-think, full-res), Lingshu-7B genuinely and ORDER-ROBUSTLY outperforms Lingshu-32B on MMMU H&M val. The +26 vs the Lingshu paper's own 7B number (54.0) is a 7B-AND-MMMU-specific unreconciled protocol/version (possible train-set-leakage) difference, NOT a bug in our eval.

evidence.parsing_clean: both models emit clean single letters ('B.','A'); parser is exact letter-match; 7B-right/32B-wrong cases are genuinely image-dependent questions the 7B answers correctly

discordance_identity.interpretation: 7B-wins vs 32B-wins = 34 vs 9 discordant pairs -> the 7B advantage is highly significant, not sampling noise

position_bias_test_cyclic_permutation.method: re-ran BOTH models on the same 150 Qs under EVERY cyclic shift of the options (shift0=original order=faithful baseline); position-debiased acc = per-question mean over shifts; per-sample dumps in mmmu_perm_{7b,32b}.json
position_bias_test_cyclic_permutation.conclusion: Position/letter bias explains only ~4 of the ~18 identity-gap points. After FULL cyclic debiasing the 7B STILL beats the 32B by ~+0.14 (0.771 vs 0.632). => the win is order-robust and is NOT a position-bias artifact.
position_bias_test_cyclic_permutation.note_identity_vs_dumps: re-run identity (7B .827 / 32B .647) is ~2-4 questions above the canonical dumps (.80/.6333); benign vLLM batch-composition / unseeded parser tie-break drift; same regime, does not affect conclusions

does_7b_still_beat_32b.answer: YES. Under every faithful lens (raw dump, re-run identity, and rigorous position-debiased), 7B > 32B on MMMU-medical val. The task's expectation that a fix would flip it is NOT borne out empirically.

method_impact.headline_metric: accuracy-max (v2) pooled SAMPLE-WEIGHTED acc vs always-32B-THINK, full suite n=42374
method_impact.sample_weighted_headline_sensitivity: MMMU is only 0.35% of pooled samples -> keep-7B vs escalate-32B moves the sample-weighted accuracy-max headline only -0.0005 (from +0.0212 to +0.0207 vs 32B-think). The headline is CARRIED BY PMC fusion + open-text verifier, NOT by the MMMU anomaly.

macro_average_sensitivity.note: MACRO (equal-weight per benchmark) IS materially inflated by keep-7B MMMU: full-suite macro drops +0.0777 -> +0.0621; MCQ-only macro is MMMU-DOMINATED, collapsing +0.0270 -> +0.0036. Any per-benchmark-equal-weight framing must correct the MMMU cell.

recommendation.for_the_method: Do NOT bank the MMMU keep-7B as a headline 'beat-32B' win. Either (a) EXCLUDE MMMU from headline claims (as the project already does for the MedVLThinker family), or (b) conservatively ESCALATE MMMU to the 32B. Justification: although the 7B empirically wins on our eval, its 0.80 is +26 over the Lingshu paper's own 7B number and cannot be reconciled -> it is not a defensible comparable baseline for a reviewer.
recommendation.headline_is_safe: On the reported SAMPLE-WEIGHTED accuracy-max headline (+0.0212 vs 32B-think), escalating/excluding MMMU changes it by only ~-0.0005 (to ~+0.0207). The headline does NOT depend on the MMMU anomaly.
recommendation.macro_must_be_fixed: If any macro / per-benchmark-averaged number is reported, recompute it with MMMU escalated: MCQ-only macro falls from +0.027 to +0.004; full-suite macro from +0.078 to +0.062.
